q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of paneer per kg?
title: Paneer carbon footprint per kg
short: Multiply the milk used per kg of paneer, from your yield records, by a milk factor; milk is most of the total. Add boiler fuel for heating, electricity for pressing, chilling and storage, the coagulant and packaging. Divide by kilograms of paneer packed.

ul: Paneer takes several kilograms of milk per kilogram, depending on fat and solids; use your own yield.
Ask your milk supplier or dairy union for a per-litre farm figure, or use a database value and name it.
Whey is a co-product. If you sell it, allocate between paneer and whey by mass of solids or by value, and state the method.
Boiler or direct-fired heating to bring milk to coagulation temperature.
Electricity for presses, chillers and cold rooms.

p: Divide by paneer packed. If you also make curd or ghee in the same plant, allocate energy by product using metered lines or batch times.

example.title: Worked example: dairy paneer line per kg (one month)
lines: Boiler PNG: 6,000 SCM x 2.05 = 12,300 kg CO2
Plant total: 30,050 / 30,000 = 1.00 kg CO2 per kg
Add milk (your yield x milk factor), citric acid and packaging
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
